newsitem.title: USA: E.W. Blanch says buys Swire unit.
newsitem.headline: E.W. Blanch says buys Swire unit.

text.p: E.W. Blanch Holdings Inc agreed to buy 70 percent of Swire Fraser Holdings Ltd, a London insurance concern, for $13.1 million, said Blanch and Swire Fraser parent Swire Pacific Limited, of Hong Kong.
Blanch also bought an additional 20-percent interest in the existing Swire Blanch Holdings Ltd International reinsurance broking joint venture, the companies said.

The combined operations of Swire Fraser and Swire Blanch will be merged into a single operation under the Swire Blanch name, which will be 70-percent owned by Blanch and 30-percent owned by Swire Pacific, the companies said.
The total $13.1-million consideration includes the assumption of certain Swire Fraser debt of $10.2 million and a cash payment of $2.9 million, they said.

The combined Swire Fraser and Swire Blanch operations had revenues of $36.9 million in 1996 and showed a loss primarily due to recognition of charges associated with the Lloyd's Reconstruction and Reconciliation Agreement and reserves for real estate no longer occupied by Swire Fraser, they said.
"The acquisition gives EWB greater access to both Lloyd's and the London Company Market," said Blanch chief executive and chairman Ted Blanch.
Blanch said it will integrate the new Swire Blanch into its enterprise. Cory Moulton will been named Swire Blanch president and chief operating officer and will report directly to Ted Blanch.

Blanch is a provider of risk management and distribution services, including reinsurance intermediary services, risk management consulting and administration services and wholesale insurance services.
Swire Pacific is a multi-national conglomerate with interests in aviation, property, offshore oil, consumer goods, shipping and trading.
